items.title: AMWA BCP-004: NMOS Capabilities
items.text: This repository holds the suite overview for the BCP-004 series of AMWA Best Common Practices, part of the family of Networked Media Open Specifications from the Advanced Media Workflow Association.

items.title: What does the suite do?
items.text:
• The BCP-004 series defines how NMOS Senders and Receivers express parametric capabilities and constraints.
  • It establishes how Controllers use those capabilities when evaluating possible connections and active constraints.

items.title: Why does it matter?
items.text:
• Controllers need to know whether a Sender and Receiver can interoperate before attempting a connection.
  • A consistent capability model allows implementations to describe supported stream parameters without vendor-specific conventions.

items.title: What are the recommendations?
items.text:
• BCP-004-01: NMOS Receiver Capabilities
  • BCP-004-02: NMOS Sender Capabilities

items.title: Getting started
items.text:
Start with the BCP relevant to the endpoint being described:

  • BCP-004-01 for Receivers
  • BCP-004-02 for Senders

There is more information about the NMOS Specifications and their GitHub repositories at https://specs.amwa.tv/nmos.

items.title: Introduction
items.text:
The BCP-004 series defines how NMOS Senders and Receivers express parametric capabilities and constraints. It provides a consistent model for describing the stream parameters an endpoint can produce or consume and for evaluating compatibility before a connection is made.

The suite is divided into two complementary recommendations:

  • BCP-004-01: NMOS Receiver Capabilities covers the capabilities and constraint sets expressed by Receivers.
  • BCP-004-02: NMOS Sender Capabilities covers the capabilities and constraint sets expressed by Senders.

The recommendations use the NMOS Parameter Registers and the IS-04 caps attribute. They should be read alongside:

  • IS-04: NMOS Discovery and Registration
  • IS-05: NMOS Device Connection Management
  • IS-11: NMOS Network Media Configuration
  • NMOS Parameter Registers
